note: Numbers for the Megabonk-style systems (movement, hordes). One row per value; verified becomes true once it feels right in game. Generated as RiskOfBonk.Generated.Tune.<PascalCaseId>.

rows.note: Megabonk has no sprint: always at full speed while moving (RoR2 still stops sprint when moving backwards or during some skills). The Sprint key becomes Slide.
Top running speed from input (maxRunSpeed 10 x MoveSpeedMultiplier). Risk of Rain 2 speed items scale it. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Acceleration from input on the ground (moveSpeed force 2700 x fixed step 0.02). Input along a direction stops pushing once you already go faster than run_speed that way. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Counter-movement on the ground: speed in a direction you are not pushing fades at this rate (counterMovement 0.25 x 54). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

On the ground, speed above run_speed fades at this rate while you keep moving (slowDownSpeed 0.01 x 54): momentum lasts. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).
Same, when you let go of the movement keys (slowDownSpeed 0.1 x 54). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

After landing, no counter-movement or speed fade for this long (justLandedCounter 15 ticks), so a quick jump keeps all your speed (bunny hop). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Steering in the air (0.45 x run_accel). Like on the ground it cannot push you past run_speed, and never slows you (air_drag does that, slowly). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

In the air, speed you are not steering along (all of it with no input) fades at this rate: Megabonk's MovementTick pushes against the look-relative velocity on each axis without input by airDeceleration 0.003 x moveSpeed 2700 x 0.02 (about 16% per second).

Jump launch speed (JumpHeight stat 7 x mass as an impulse). Jumping while still rising halves the old upward speed first. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Megabonk's gravity (Physics gravity -19.62); Risk of Rain 2 uses 30, so players fall slower and jumps hang longer. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Speed added when a slide starts (slideForce 200 x 0.02), only if you went faster than slide_boost_min_speed since the last slide. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).
slideThresholdSpeed: the next slide boost is ready once you reach this speed. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).
Time before another slide can boost (slideCooldownCounterMax 25 ticks). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).
Speed lost per second while sliding (slideCounterMovement 0.1 x 54), the same at any speed. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Sliding downhill speeds you up by gravity along the slope (Megabonk's rigidbody has no friction while sliding); uphill slows you. Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Sideways steering while sliding (forward input does nothing in a slide; sideways input pushes at run_accel). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).

Holding Slide below slide_boost_min_speed crouches instead of sliding, and a slide that slows down to this becomes a crouch; crouching caps your speed at this x run speed (Megabonk's CheckInput: GetMaxSpeed x 0.5 while crouched).
Climbing speed up a wall: max(this, 1.5 x run speed) (minWallClimbSpeed 10). Megabonk's PlayerMovement.WallClimbing / CanWallClimb (GameAssembly), Monke's WallClimb passive only.
Speed pressing you into the wall while climbing. Megabonk's PlayerMovement.WallClimbing / CanWallClimb (GameAssembly), Monke's WallClimb passive only.
After a climb ends, the next one waits this long (wallClimbCooldown). Megabonk's PlayerMovement.WallClimbing / CanWallClimb (GameAssembly), Monke's WallClimb passive only.
You climb when your movement points at the wall within this angle (wallrunAttachAngle). Megabonk's PlayerMovement.WallClimbing / CanWallClimb (GameAssembly), Monke's WallClimb passive only.
Safety cap on horizontal speed (Megabonk has none; this only stops runaway physics). Measured from Megabonk (GameAssembly: PlayerMovement / PlayerMovementValues, 50 Hz physics).
Monster spawn budget over time (stage and Teleporter directors without a boss squad).
Most monsters one director wave may spawn (RoR2 default 6). Cheap monsters are no longer skipped.
Time between director waves.
Non-boss monsters are weaker so the horde mows down like in Megabonk.
Extra monster credit for the Teleporter's horde director when the Megabonk boss event starts.
Monster team soft limit (RoR2 default 40).
Invincibility while the level-up menu is open; ends early when you pick. The countdown turns red and shakes in its last 30%.
Chance that a level-up card is a Megabonk weapon (Megabonk survivors only), otherwise a tome.
A chest opened by a Megabonk survivor holds a Megabonk upgrade (a bonus pick: the level-up menu with weapons and tomes) instead of its item this often (src/Chests.cs). Item chests only.
XP in each gem compared with Risk of Rain 2's own kill XP (Megabonk levels up more often).
XP gems within this distance of a player fly to them and are collected.
Most gems on the ground; past this the oldest gem is collected for the team at once.
Megabonk Charge Shrines placed on each normal stage (with a Teleporter), next to Risk of Rain 2's own shrines.
Time a player must stand inside a Charge Shrine to charge it fully. Leaving pauses the charge (it slowly drains).
Radius of a Charge Shrine's circle.
Upgrade picks every player gets when a Charge Shrine is fully charged.
Megabonk Magnet Shrines per stage: stand in one briefly and every XP gem on the map flies to you.
Time to stand in a Magnet Shrine to use it.
Time to stand in a Moai, Greed or Challenge Shrine to use it.
Megabonk Moai Shrines per stage: every player gets a random tome at a rolled rarity (luck helps).
Megabonk Greed Shrines per stage: more gold and more monsters for the rest of the stage.
Greed Shrine: gold from monsters spawned afterwards is multiplied by this (stacks per shrine).
Greed Shrine: the stage's monster directors earn this much more credit (stacks per shrine).
Megabonk Challenge Shrines per stage: a champion wave; kill it and every player gets an upgrade pick.
Challenge Shrine budget, times the run's difficulty coefficient: a champion from the stage's monsters that fits (elite when it can), else the usual Shrine of Combat pick (which uses 100).
Megabonk Cursed Shrines per stage (our reading of Megabonk's curse: risk for reward).
Upgrade picks every player gets from a Cursed Shrine.
Cursed Shrine: the stage's monster directors earn this much more credit, and elites cost half as much, for the rest of the stage.
Monster credit per second for the Megabonk swarm during a final boss fight (Mithrix/Ghost King, False Son/Shadow King, Voidling), times the square root of the difficulty coefficient.
Colour saturation added on stages (Megabonk's bright colours).
Contrast added on stages.
Brightness added on stages (HDR grading, which the stages checked use: lakes, foggyswamp, sulfurpools, dampcavesimple).
Brightness added on stages that grade in LDR (none of the stages checked so far).
Stage fog strength is multiplied by this. 1 = unchanged: lighter fog made Risk of Rain 2's stages darker (their fog carries much of the light).
Above this ground speed the run clip plays instead of idle. Ours: Megabonk's Animator transitions are not read.
In the air, rising faster than this plays the jump clip, otherwise the falling clip. Ours: Megabonk's Animator transitions are not read.
Crossfade time between clips. Ours: Megabonk's Animator transitions are not read.
A clip change has to be wanted this long before it happens (jumps start at once), so walking at the edge of run speed does not flicker. Ours: Megabonk's Animator transitions are not read.
Volume of Megabonk's sounds, on top of Risk of Rain 2's master and sound effect volume.
Megabonk's music (MegabonkMusic) plays at the game's master x music volume times this.

rows.unit: x base damage per Megabonk damage point
rows.note: Megabonk weapon damage (mbDamage in weapons.json, e.g. Revolver 5 per bullet, Sniper 22) times this is the hit's damage coefficient in Risk of Rain 2 (x the body's base damage). Keeps Megabonk's balance between weapons; this value sets the overall strength.

What a Risk of Rain 2 survivor's own kit deals per second, in units of its base damage, counting each extra enemy a hit reaches (Commando: Double Tap about 5/s, Phase Round and Suppressive Fire about 1.7/s more, little area). A Megabonk survivor's weapons are scaled towards this so they are as strong as the Risk of Rain 2 survivors next to them; RoR2 items, levels and tomes then grow both alike.

rows.unit: x reference power per weapon level
rows.note: Each weapon level a Megabonk survivor gains (a new weapon is one level, an upgrade pick adds its rarity's levels) raises the power its weapons may reach by this much of the reference: a little less than one Damage Tome point (8%), since a Megabonk survivor's weapons also reach more enemies, so a weapon pick and a tome pick are worth the same and Risk of Rain 2 survivors (who take only tomes) keep up.

How strongly the weapons are pulled to the allowed power: 1 makes every loadout exactly as strong, lower lets strong weapon choices stay a little stronger (power = allowed^strength x raw^(1-strength)).
Weak loadouts are raised at most this much (most are lowered).

Enemies a melee swing hits on average in a horde (used to compare its power). Lowered to 1.5: Risk of Rain 2 monsters often fight from range (a Lemurian spits fireballs before it bites), so close-range weapons reach fewer of them than in Megabonk's melee hordes (test bot: Megachad took 144 damage in 10 s while dealing 9 per second).

Enemies an aura hits on average in a horde. Lowered to 1.5: Risk of Rain 2 monsters often fight from range (a Lemurian spits fireballs before it bites), so close-range weapons reach fewer of them than in Megabonk's melee hordes (test bot: Megachad took 144 damage in 10 s while dealing 9 per second).
Enemies a projectile hits on average (some explode, bounce or return).
Enemies a lightning strike reaches on average (it chains).
Enemies a piercing bullet hits on average (Sniper, Space Noodle); other bullets hit one.

Megabonk's StageSummoner.GetNumTargetEnemies: the enemies it keeps alive start at 5 + 200 x (stage time / stageDuration), times (1 + 0.4 x stage) here (Megabonk: 1 + 0.7 x Difficulty + 0.4 x its stage multiplier). This is the 5.
Megabonk's +200 enemies over a stage (GetNumTargetEnemies).
Megabonk's stageDuration (MapData, Forest: 600 s): the target ramps over this long.
Each stage cleared raises the target by this much of itself (Megabonk's 0.4 x stage multiplier).

Risk of Rain 2 monsters are tougher, smarter and much heavier to run than Megabonk's, so the target is this share of Megabonk's (about 30 alive at 4 minutes, the horde_limit cap by 10), never above horde_limit.

rows.unit: credits per missing monster per s
rows.note: While fewer monsters are alive than the target, each monster director without a boss squad earns this much extra credit per missing monster per second (a Lemurian costs 11, a Beetle 8), so the horde fills up like Megabonk's.

On Bonk style stages Risk of Rain 2's ranged monsters (MegabonkEnemies.Ranged: wisps, Clay Templars, Alloy Vultures, Solus Probes, Hermit Crabs, Brass Contraptions, lunar and void shooters...) spawn this much as often: Megabonk's hordes are melee chasers, and its looks on them are melee enemies. Close-range survivors (Megachad's aura) need the enemies to come to them.
